NDT training in Little Rock: how it works for Little Rock employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Little Rock employers and technicians is delivered by Atlantis NDT as live online theory plus onsite practical sessions at your own facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification itself follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A, so it is employer-based: your company's written practice sets the training and experience requirements, a Level III gives the general, specific and practical exams, and the employer signs the certificate. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Little Rock; the course comes to your crew or to your screen.

That model suits central Arkansas better than most people expect. The work here is spread out: pipe production and steel fabrication along the Arkansas River, aircraft completion at the airport, locomotive overhaul across the river in North Little Rock, and outage or turnaround calls that send technicians to Russellville, El Dorado or the Mississippi County steel mills. Pulling a whole crew out of that schedule for a week at a distant schoolhouse is expensive. Training the crew at the plant, on the plant's own parts and procedures, keeps people productive and gives the auditor a cleaner file.

SNT-TC-1A elementWho sets itWhat a Little Rock employer keeps on file
Formal training hoursYour written practice, using the SNT-TC-1A recommended minimums as a floorCourse outline, attendance record, instructor signature
On-the-job experienceYour written practice, by method and levelSigned OJT log with dates, techniques and supervising Level II/III

The hour and experience figures for each method and level are laid out in the NDT training requirements matrix; we link to it rather than repeating numbers here because your written practice may set them higher than the recommended minimums.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Little Rock

Every course below is built on ASNT SNT-TC-1A and the matching ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outline, and every course can be delivered as live online theory, onsite at a Little Rock-area facility, or a blend of the two. The right-hand columns describe how the method is typically used around central Arkansas and what a trainee should have before starting.

MethodLevelsWhat Little Rock employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, IIWeld seam and plate body inspection on large-diameter pipe, thickness surveys on tanks and piping, structural weld checks for fabricatorsLevel I: none beyond basic maths. Level II: Level I UT plus documented OJT
Phased Array UT (PAUT)IIEncoded weld scans where radiography would hold up production or clear an area; corrosion mapping on vessels and tanksUT Level II (or equivalent UT theory and OJT)
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)IIThick-section weld sizing on pressure equipment and heavy fabrications; pairs with PAUT on code-case inspectionsUT Level II
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, IIWeld radiography on pipe, pressure vessels and pipelines; film or digital interpretationRadiation safety training plus Arkansas licensing requirements for anyone handling sources
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, IISurface crack detection on locomotive components, structural steel, castings and forgingsNone for Level I; MT Level I plus OJT for Level II
Penetrant Testing (PT)I, IINon-magnetic parts, aerospace fittings and aluminium structure, stainless weldsNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, IIWeld and fit-up inspection in fabrication shops, bridge and structural surveys, pre-NDT surface checksNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, IIAircraft structure and fastener-hole inspection, conductivity checks, tubing inspection in heat exchangersBasic electrical theory; ET Level I plus OJT for Level II

Most central Arkansas employers start with a core of UT, MT and VT, then add RT or PAUT as their customer specifications demand. Aerospace-facing shops add PT and ET. If you are not sure which method or level to begin with, request a Little Rock training quote and describe the work; we will suggest a sequence rather than sell you every course at once.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Little Rock, step by step

  1. Confirm the employer's written practice. Under SNT-TC-1A, certification belongs to the employer. If your Little Rock company does not yet have a written practice, or it has not been reviewed since the 2024 edition of SNT-TC-1A, that comes first; see written practice development.
  2. Complete formal (classroom) training. Theory is delivered live online or onsite. The hours your written practice requires per method and level are in the requirements matrix.
  3. Build on-the-job experience. The trainee works under a certified Level II or III on real production, and every session is logged with the technique used and the supervisor's signature.
  4. Pass the general exam. A written test on method principles, administered or approved by the Level III.
  5. Pass the specific exam. A written test on your equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria, which is where a pipe mill's exam and an aircraft completion centre's exam look very different.
  6. Pass the practical exam. Hands-on testing of real specimens with known flaws, graded by a Level III against a checklist. This cannot be done remotely.
  7. Pass the vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, repeated annually under most written practices.
  8. Receive employer certification. The employer certifies the technician on the Level III's recommendation, and the file is closed for audit.
  9. Recertify on schedule. Recertification intervals and criteria are set in the written practice; plan them before a customer audit asks.

For the employer-side programme (written practice, exams, records and Level III of record) see the SNT-TC-1A training and certification page.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Little Rock crews

Atlantis does not operate a training centre in Little Rock or anywhere else in Arkansas. Training is delivered in three honest ways:

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions with questions answered in real time, scheduled around shift patterns. Theory covers the formal-training component of SNT-TC-1A; it does not replace practical training or the practical exam. Details on NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led session at your plant, shop or yard, using your instruments, your procedures and your own parts as specimens where suitable. This is usually the best value for a crew of several technicians.
  • Blended. Theory online first, then a concentrated practical block onsite. This works well for companies whose technicians are spread across Little Rock, Pine Bluff, Conway and job sites further afield.

Scheduling follows your calendar, not ours. Spring and autumn outage seasons at power plants and the turnaround window at refineries pull central Arkansas technicians away for weeks; we plan cohorts either side of those windows. Pipe mills and fabrication shops with steady production often prefer short onsite blocks between orders. Ask about onsite training for your Little Rock crew and we will send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Larger programmes covering several sites or methods are handled through corporate NDT training, which adds a single training plan, consolidated records and Level III oversight across locations.

Where NDT technicians work in Little Rock

Central Arkansas is not a single-industry market, which is why technicians here tend to carry more than one method. The sectors that generate steady inspection work include:

  • Pipe and steel products. Large-diameter pipe production and structural steel fabrication along the Port of Little Rock industrial area, with customers who specify API 5L pipe requirements, AWS D1.1 for structural welds and ASME Section V for NDT techniques.
  • Steel mills in northeast Arkansas. Mississippi County, around Blytheville and Osceola, is home to major steel production. Maintenance and expansion work there calls for UT, MT and VT on cranes, rolls, structures and pressure equipment.
  • Aerospace and aircraft completion. Business-jet completion and maintenance at Bill and Hillary Clinton National Airport generates PT, ET and VT demand, usually to customer and OEM specifications layered on SNT-TC-1A.
  • Rail. Locomotive and component overhaul in North Little Rock relies on MT and UT for axles, frames and welded repairs.
  • Power and nuclear. Outages at power plants within driving range, including the nuclear station at Russellville, bring short, intense demand for UT, ET, VT and RT technicians. Nuclear work is often governed by additional programme requirements beyond SNT-TC-1A, so check the plant's qualification rules before you commit.
  • Oil, gas and pipelines. The south Arkansas refinery at El Dorado, natural gas gathering systems in north-central Arkansas, and interstate pipelines crossing the state need weld radiography and UT to API 1104 and ASME B31 codes.
  • Bridges and infrastructure. The Arkansas Department of Transportation and its consultants inspect steel bridges across the river system. The 2021 fracture found in a tie girder of the I-40 Hernando de Soto Bridge between West Memphis and Memphis made fracture-critical inspection a live topic across the region, and VT, MT and UT remain the core methods.
  • Defense manufacturing. The Camden area in south Arkansas hosts defense and munitions manufacturers whose suppliers need documented, auditable NDT personnel qualification.

Radiography licensing in Arkansas

Arkansas is an NRC Agreement State, so the state, not the NRC, licenses most radioactive material used for industrial radiography. The programme sits with the Arkansas Department of Health, Radiation Control Section. In practice that means a Little Rock RT company needs a state radioactive-material licence for its gamma sources (and registration for X-ray equipment), and each radiographer must meet the radiographer certification and training requirements in the state rules, which follow the NRC's industrial radiography framework: radiation safety training, a recognised radiographer certification, personal dosimetry, survey meters and the two-person rule at temporary job sites. Out-of-state crews working in Arkansas typically need reciprocity through the Radiation Control Section before they start.

Atlantis RT courses cover the method, technique and interpretation required for SNT-TC-1A certification and include radiation safety principles, but an NDT course is not a radiation licence. Your company's Radiation Safety Officer and the state programme remain the authority on who may handle sources.

Method spotlight: ultrasonic testing on welded pipe and plate

If one method defines Little Rock's inspection market, it is UT on welded steel pipe and plate. Large-diameter pipe for pipelines and water transmission is made with long submerged-arc weld seams, and pipe specifications require those seams and the plate body to be examined, typically by automated ultrasonic systems with manual UT and radiography used to prove up indications and check pipe ends.

For a technician, that means a UT Level II here is not only about reading an A-scan on a calibration block. The specific exam and the practical will usually cover:

  • Angle-beam technique on longitudinal and helical seams, including how curvature changes beam path and skip distance.
  • Reference standards with notches and drilled holes, and how automated system sensitivity is set and verified against them.
  • Lamination checks on plate and pipe ends, where straight-beam UT is the primary tool.
  • Prove-up of automated indications with manual UT and how results are recorded for the mill's quality system.
  • Where PAUT and TOFD fit when a customer asks for encoded, auditable data instead of a pass/fail stamp.

The same UT skill set transfers directly to structural fabricators, steel mills and pipeline contractors in the state, which is why it is the most portable certification a central Arkansas technician can hold. Practice questions are on the UT Level 2 practice questions page.

Level III services and written practices for Little Rock NDT companies

Training only counts if it sits inside a compliant programme. For Little Rock inspection companies, fabricators and plant owners we provide:

  • Written practice development and review aligned with SNT-TC-1A, so your training hours, OJT, exams, vision tests and recertification rules are defined before the first certificate is signed. See written practice development.
  • Level III exam administration for general, specific and practical exams, with graded records your auditor can follow.
  • Procedure and technique review against the codes your customers cite (ASME Section V, AWS D1.1, API 1104 and others).
  • Level III of record support for companies that do not employ a full-time Level III.

Consulting and training are linked on purpose. If you need inspection-programme or Level III consulting rather than a course, see NDT Level III consulting in Little Rock or the statewide Arkansas NDT consulting page. For every Arkansas city we cover, the state hub is NDT training in Arkansas. Book a Level III consultation if you want to talk through your programme first.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical exams are where trainees most often stumble, usually because they have had limited time on equipment. The Practical NDT simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in 5 realistic 3D environments (an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank) before they ever touch the real specimens. It is useful between theory and the practical block, and for refreshing skills before recertification. There is also a Practical NDT page for Little Rock.

Be clear on its limits: the simulator is practice only. It does not replace hands-on training, OJT hours or the practical examination on real specimens, which must be graded by a Level III.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Little Rock

How do I get NDT certified in Little Rock?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A you are certified by an employer, not by a school. You complete formal training in a method, build documented on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams given or approved by a Level III, pass a vision test and are then certified by the employer under its written practice. Atlantis delivers the training and can support the exams and written practice; the certificate is your employer's.

Can I take NDT training online in Arkansas?

Yes, for theory. Live online sessions cover the formal-training component and are scheduled around shifts. The practical training and the practical exam still have to be done in person on real parts, either onsite at your employer's facility or at an arranged venue. See NDT training online for how this works.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your written practice, your prior UT Level I training and how quickly you can build documented OJT. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum formal-training hours and experience for each level, and many employers set higher figures. The exact recommended numbers are in the training requirements matrix; the experience component usually takes longer than the classroom component.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Arkansas?

Industrial radiography with radioactive sources is licensed through the Arkansas Department of Health, Radiation Control Section, because Arkansas is an NRC Agreement State. Your employer holds the licence; radiographers and assistants must meet the state's training and certification requirements. An NDT course alone does not authorise you to handle sources.

What does NDT training cost in Little Rock?

We do not publish prices because the right answer depends on the method, the level, the number of technicians, whether training is online, onsite or blended, and whether you need exam administration or written-practice support as well. Request a Little Rock training quote and we will reply with cohort and onsite quotes within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Little Rock employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used qualification framework in US industry, and the central Arkansas employers described above generally work to it or to customer specifications that reference it. Remember that SNT-TC-1A certification is employer-specific: if you change employers, the new employer recertifies you under its own written practice, though your documented training and experience carry over.

Can you train our crew at our Little Rock plant?

Yes. Onsite delivery at your facility is our most common format for employer cohorts. We use your equipment and procedures where they are suitable, plan around production and outages, and leave you with training and exam records ready for audit.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training?

Both programmes require training from an approved provider. GI Bill benefits apply only to programmes approved for VA education benefits through the state approving agency, and WIOA funding generally requires a provider listed on the state's Eligible Training Provider List, which in Arkansas is accessed through Arkansas Workforce Centers. Atlantis does not claim either approval. The route that works for most technicians is employer-paid training: your employer or prospective employer sponsors the course as part of certifying you under its written practice. A college programme such as SAU Tech's may be the better choice if you want to use education benefits.

Do I need a college degree to work in NDT?

No. SNT-TC-1A allows certification based on training and experience, with some reduction in experience requirements for relevant technical education. A degree helps for Level III and engineering roles, but most Level I and II technicians qualify through training and OJT.

Which methods should I start with in central Arkansas?

UT, MT and VT cover the broadest range of local work across pipe, steel, rail and fabrication. Add RT for pipeline and pressure-vessel work, and PT and ET if you want to work around aircraft. Pay information by level and method is in the NDT salary guide.

Can Atlantis help us prepare a technician for Level III?

Yes. Level III preparation covers the Basic exam (materials, processes and general NDT knowledge), the method exams and the practical and procedure-writing skills a Level III needs. See ASNT Level III training.

Do you offer API, CWI or ISO 9712 courses?

No. Our training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Some Little Rock fabricators and refinery contractors also ask for AWS CWI or API inspector credentials, and those are separate schemes run by their own bodies. We are happy to explain how they sit alongside an SNT-TC-1A certification.

Talk to us about NDT training in Little Rock, browse every course on the NDT training page, or request a cohort quote for your team.
